faqs.question: Which type of AI video tool do I need?
faqs.answer: Choose by workflow first. Generative video tools create or transform footage; avatar-video tools turn scripts into presenter-style videos; screen-recording platforms capture walkthroughs and explainers. These categories overlap only partly, so compare products that solve the same task.

faqs.question: How much do AI video tools cost?
faqs.answer: Current prices and plan limits are not independently verified in this entry. Check each vendor’s pricing page and calculate the cost using your expected creators, generation credits or recording minutes, storage, exports, and collaboration seats.

faqs.question: What should I test before choosing a generative video tool?
faqs.answer: Use the same prompts and source assets across shortlisted tools. Score prompt adherence, motion consistency, visual artifacts, editing effort, export quality, generation speed, and whether the license permits your intended commercial use.

faqs.question: What should a team check before adopting a screen-recording tool?
faqs.answer: Test recording length, transcript accuracy, sharing permissions, viewer access, retention, export, and any AI summaries using real but non-sensitive examples. Confirm which controls are included in the plan you would purchase.

faqs.question: Are the ratings and prices in this comparison verified?
faqs.answer: No. Ratings and prices in this entry have not been independently verified for this update. Treat them as unavailable and confirm current features, terms, and pricing with each vendor before making a decision.

faqs.question: How were these tools selected?
faqs.answer: This is a practical shortlist organized by workflow fit and the criteria listed above, not a claim that every product was independently tested or that the listed ratings were verified. Run your own side-by-side evaluation before choosing.

faqs.question: What about privacy and commercial-use rights?
faqs.answer: Review each vendor’s data processing terms, retention and training settings, access controls, copyright and commercial-use terms, and any consent requirements for real people or likenesses. Requirements differ by product and plan.
